# Owner manual acceptance feedback (2026-11-06): YallaFlow — Manual Acceptance UX Findings

During the consolidated v1.2.0 / v1.3.0 manual review the owner identified missing product capabilities: the Console shows Flow and Agent activity but lacks complete project management and onboarding. Goal: a practical engineering workspace, not a workflow viewer with chat. Investigate and propose a cohesive solution:

1. Work Item Management: create/browse; open, edit and manage requirements under existing change-control rules; explicit activate/switch; pause, resume, close via supported lifecycle operations; move between Flow stages only when canonical Core rules permit; show why a move is blocked and the next action; contextual actions and drag-and-drop where safe. Stages are not arbitrary Kanban columns; never change stage flags directly, fabricate evidence, bypass reviews, or duplicate Core rules. Determine which actions exist in the CLI and which need new supported Core operations.
2. Existing Project Onboarding and Overview: detect an approved baseline; otherwise offer onboarding/scan via the existing discovery process; detect the real stack from repository evidence (backend, frontend, database, frameworks, build tools, package managers, environment configuration); distinguish confirmed/inferred/unknown; require review and approval before inferred information becomes authoritative memory. Project Overview: description/purpose, stack, structure, onboarding and memory status, work status and integrity warnings, development environment status, Run/Stop/Logs where safely supported. Two meanings of start/stop kept separate: (A) pausing/resuming YallaFlow project activity, (B) starting/stopping local development services (Laravel, Node.js, Docker). Never execute an inferred shell command without explicit confirmation; investigate process ownership, safe termination, environment variables, ports, logging, restart.
3. New Project Wizard: name and location, optional description, stack choice, supported starter templates or agent recommendation, database/frontend/backend options, preview of structure and setup steps, controlled auditable creation, YallaFlow init and initial workflow. No hardcoded "best stack"; reuse framework generators/templates rather than a second scaffolding engine.
4. UX Integration: keep visual identity and Flow; one coherent experience: Project Overview, Flow/Work Management, Agent Workspace, Evidence and Delivery, Project Setup/Development Runtime; no overload with developer commands or raw configuration; clear first run for existing and new projects.
5. Architecture and Release Scope: inspect the actual v1.2.0 and v1.3.0 candidates; what existing Core commands cover versus significant new infrastructure; classify into essential fixes for the current release, small improvements that fit the current scope, major additions for the next minor release; honest assessment, not automatic scope expansion; complexity, security, backward compatibility, tests.
6. Deliverables: UX gap analysis; Core capability inventory; user journeys (old and new projects); task-management interaction design; Project Overview and stack detection design; Project Runner safety and lifecycle design; New Project Wizard design; visual prototype or mockup; prioritized roadmap and release recommendation.

Use existing YallaFlow governance and record the findings as manual acceptance feedback. Do not modify production projects or execute application startup commands during research. Do not commit, tag, push or publish. Stop after presenting the proposed architecture, UX and release impact for review.
